A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARGenSeg and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete scientific appendices A–F. V2 adds a NeurIPS checklist before the retained appendices; this does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation, multimodal understanding, generation, efficiency, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including ARGenSeg benchmark scores, timing measurements, qualitative outputs, and controlled ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same architecture, frozen visual tokenizer, direct visual-token prediction, cross-entropy training, and next-scale inference procedure. The added checklist does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Training coverage in Table 7 and evaluation coverage throughout Section 4 and the appendices are unchanged, including referring and interactive segmentation, multimodal understanding, and ImageNet-based image generation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including HiMTok in segmentation comparisons, InternVL2.5 understanding controls, and SAM-B, SAM-L, and PSALM in interactive segmentation.

E3.justification: The versions retain identical sample sizes, splits, metrics, training budgets, output resolution, and inference-timing settings. Checklist assertions about experimental details add no new protocol or revision to an existing setting.

E4.justification: The understanding-data, projector, pretraining, tokenizer, backbone, and diffusion-head ablations are unchanged. Appendix control experiments and qualitative comparisons in Figures 5–7 are also retained without additions or removals.

E5.justification: The new checklist, item 7, explicitly discloses that error bars are omitted because of resource limitations. This is a limited reporting disclosure: no uncertainty estimates, significance tests, seeds, or repeated-run counts are added.

E6.justification: All corresponding numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, ARGenSeg retains 82.2 RefCOCO-val cIoU in Table 1, 72.4 average performance in Table 2, and 1.28 seconds per image in Table 4; appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–3 are unchanged apart from spacing. Neither version contains theoretical results or proofs; the new checklist merely states their absence.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified segmentation without dedicated segmentation heads, direct visual-token prediction, segmentation performance, and efficient coarse-to-fine generation.

C2.justification: Checklist items 7 and 11 newly acknowledge resource constraints behind missing error bars and the current absence of model-release safeguards. Existing result interpretations, applicability discussions, and limitations in Appendices E–F remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page footnote stating code availability and identifying the ARGenSeg repository; v1 has no equivalent code-access pointer. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning, and all 78 bibliographic references are unchanged. The added checklist's policy links do not introduce related research or revise the claimed relationship to prior methods.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a standalone NeurIPS checklist between the references and scientific appendices and identifies the corresponding author. The research narrative, section ordering, and explanations remain unchanged; most added prose is standard checklist guidance.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is slightly reduced and the first page is reflowed to accommodate the new footnote. All seven figures and ten tables retain their content, captions, and structure. The checklist shifts the scientific appendices to later pages without redesigning them.

improvement.justification: The new code-repository pointer improves access documentation, while explicit acknowledgments of missing error bars and release safeguards modestly improve transparency. The scientific evidence is unchanged. Checklist item 16's apparent inconsistency with the MLLM-based method in Section 3 weakens the added checklist, but the code-access documentation still provides a limited net benefit.
